iPadOS 27.2 will release its beta version this week. In addition to the redesigned Health app, Apple is also bringing over a recent Mac feature: a Siri window that pops up when you select text.

iPadOS 27.2 adds the feature of a Siri window popping up when text is selected, similar to macOS Golden Gate

Siri AI is the headline new feature of iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and related releases. Precisely because of this, Apple offers many different ways to invoke this brand-new, more capable assistant.

On iPad, you can activate Siri with the "Siri" or "Hey Siri" voice commands, swipe down from the top of the screen, use the new Siri option in the edit menu, open the new Siri app, or use my favourite method: press CMD + Space to bring up Spotlight, then ask Siri right there.

However, iPadOS 27.2 adds yet another option, ported directly from Mac.

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, in many situations when you select a portion of text, a small Siri icon will appear at the upper-left corner of the selection. When you hover your cursor over the icon, it expands and provides an "Ask Siri" text input field.

This feature was not available in iPadOS 27. But now, if you have a trackpad connected to your iPad, iPadOS 27.2 delivers the same experience.

As you can see from the image above, the new Siri icon starts out very small and doesn't get in the way, but simply hovering your cursor over it brings up the "Ask Siri" input field, which is very convenient.

If you don't have a trackpad connected, the full edit menu will still appear after you select text, and you can tap the option inside to open Siri. With a trackpad, however, the whole experience is smoother and more seamless.

macOS has many of these subtle productivity-focused features that can speed up everyday operations, but iPadOS has always lacked them. So it's exciting to see yet another Mac feature make its way to iPad.

What do you think of the new Siri popup in iPadOS 27.2? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
